images.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: Breachline made-people concept lineup revision, 1536 x 1024 landscape PNG.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the current PL3D six-person lineup. The creator likes this direction and asks only for somewhat more visible scarring.

Keep all SIX existing individuals in exactly the same order, with their same faces, ages, body proportions, ordinary adult scale, poses, expressions, hair, garments, matching full-body/portrait pairs, and two-row three-column composition. Preserve the painted warm ivory backdrop, matte oil/acrylic brushwork, muted colours, cold bloodless skin, old lividity, distant gazes and the woman's cloudy eye. Keep the existing scene and framing.

Change only the SCARRING. Increase the size, contrast and readable relief of their old healed scars, and add a few carefully placed scars on currently bare skin. They should be clearly noticeable at the normal sheet viewing size, not only in a close crop. Give each person a distinct history: one or two main scars with a few smaller marks, irregular rather than matching decorative patterns. Pale slightly raised or recessed healed tissue against the ashen skin, a little muted dusky colour at some edges. More evident, but do not cover every inch.
Top left: an old diagonal scar crossing one cheek and a small neck mark.
Top middle: emphasize the existing CLOSED throat scar as a broad irregular healed injury, plus a short brow scar.
Top right: a visibly healed temple/scalp injury and a few old forearm scars.
Bottom left: a healed brow/temple scar near the existing cloudy eye, and clearer collarbone scars.
Bottom middle: make the existing cheek and upper chest scars distinctly broader and more readable.
Bottom right: a clear old brow-to-cheek scar and a few healed marks on the exposed hand/forearm.
Match the visible scar placement between each full-body person and their larger portrait. Do not alter identities to accommodate scars. Retain substantial intact bodies and the sense of people returned from death at a cost.
Healed skin only: no open or bleeding wounds, exposed tissue, stitches, thread, metal staples, bolts, glowing marks, tattoo-like scar patterns or fresh gore. Do not add props, muscles or bulk. No text, numbers, captions, frames, logos or watermark. Preserve everything else from the supplied image.
images.creator_note: Rejected · stronger scarring went too far; PL3D is final.

His matching small full-body figure must likewise have two natural non-cloudy eyes.
Do NOT touch the BOTTOM LEFT woman's existing cloudy eye; it is intentional and must stay. Do NOT fade, remove or add scars. Change nothing else.

images.title: Crest folk · integrated sweep
images.summary: The crest grows more continuously through the brow and temples, with its lower sweep tapering into the nape and neck. The selected individual and slender body remain the basis; this integration is a proposal for review.

takes.title: Integrated sweep
takes.text: Continuous brow-to-crest roots and a tapered sweep into the upper neck, keeping the selected face, markings and body.
takes.handoff: The selected PL9.4/CR1 design is revised so the crest’s sweep belongs to the skull, temples and upper neck, with restrained echoes in the surrounding anatomy. This responds to the creator’s integration request; the new structure and any biological function are not final.

images.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: Breachline Crest folk reference-sheet revision, 1536 x 1024 landscape PNG.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, CR1. The creator asks: make the sweep more integrated into the overall design.

Preserve this selected adult woman's identity, slender strong body, ordinary scale, russet cheek marks, chalk-tan colour, long hands, barefoot anatomy, short plain grey-brown tunic and wrist cord. Keep the same layout: three complete body views (three-quarter/front, side, rear) on the left, large portrait, profile and hand detail on the right. Preserve the warm ivory empty backdrop, restrained traditional matte oil/acrylic paint, diffuse light and calm character.

REVISE THE CREST AS PART OF ONE COHERENT ANATOMY. Keep the distinctive swept-back fluted crest and its general size and recognisable silhouette, but integrate its sweep into the head, neck and upper-body design. Currently it reads a little like a separate thick layered headdress. Remove that attached-cap impression.
Make the brow and cheekbone planes flow naturally backward into the crest roots through continuous temple anatomy, without an abrupt rim, seam or separate scalp cap. The ridges should develop gradually out of the skull, be shallow and broad at their roots, then lift into the existing backward sweep. Reduce the stacked shelf effect a little without erasing the fluted character. Let the lower crest taper into the occiput and upper nape, with a clean elegant curve continuing down the neck toward the shoulders. The skull, jaw, neck and shoulder silhouette should feel designed together, with subtle swept planes rather than a human wearing a rigid shell.
Give the existing cheek markings a subtle backward direction that agrees with the sweep. Echo the same direction very lightly in the broad anatomical planes at collarbone/shoulder and exposed forearm, while keeping the limbs smooth and functional. Do not bolt crests onto other joints, spread folds across the whole body, add armor plates, or turn her into a reptile or sci-fi alien. This is an integrated visual gesture and a believable cranial structure, not a repeated decorative motif.
Show these same attachments and transitions consistently in EVERY view, especially profile and rear. Keep anatomy readable under the existing garment; do not change or remove clothing, add props or expose new areas. No extra limbs, tail, fins, horns, flowing flesh ribbons, jewelry, text, numbers, frames, logos or watermark. Preserve the rest of the sheet.
images.creator_note: Sweep integrated into the anatomy · revision awaiting review
